Reṇukā
------------------------------------------
Reṇukā was the foster daughter of the king Prasenajit. He had found her as a baby-girl lying on a lotus flower.
She was married to the sage जमदग्नि. She bore him five sons, of whom परशुराम was the youngest.
Once, suspecting her fidelity, जमदग्नि asked his sons one by one, to behead her. None obeyed him except परशुराम who promptly beheaded not only रेणुका but also the elder brothers, as per the command of his ड़थेर्. Pleased with his implicit obedience, जमदग्नि asked him to choose any boon. परशुराम earnestly requested him to bring them all back to life!
See also JAMADAGNI and PARAŚURĀMA.

Reṇukācārya
------------------------------------------
Śaivism (especially वीरशैविस्म्) is said to have been started originally by five great teachers known as Pañcācāryas. They are: Reṇuka, Maruḷasiddha, Ekorāma, Viśveśvara and Paṇḍitārādhya.
Reṇukācārya—also known by other names such as Revaṇasiddha and Piṇyāṅka—was considered as an इन्चर्नतिओन् of Reṇuka-गणेश, the best among the pramathagaṇas (Śiva’s retinue). He is said to have emerged out of the Someśvara-लिङ्ग at Kollipāki in Andhra Pradesh.
He toured the whole of the country of Bhārata, specially visiting the places dear to शिव or dedicated to शिव like Kāñcīpura and उज्जयिनी.
He performed many miracles like giving wealth to the poor, restoring the eyesights of the blind, feeding a large number of people with a small quantity of ड़ोओद्, saving the lives of many women who were to be sacrificed and so on.
He is supposed to have lived for 1400 years!
He was the first pontiff of the Vīrasiṁhāsana monastery at Rambhāpurī (in Karnataka State).
